question: What drives the difference between how Schwab earns on client assets and how an advisor-led model earns?

claims.text: Schwab - The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) states management's principle that developing trusted relationships will bring more assets from new and existing clients, "ultimately driving more revenue." It cites $11.90 trillion in client assets and names scale as a key advantage, because it lets Schwab spread operating costs and amortize investments over a large client base.

Schwab - In its January 2026 results release (published 2026-01-21), Schwab describes a "diversified revenue model." It reported record 2025 revenue of $23.9 billion, up 22%. It also reported that Managed Investing net inflows grew 36% and that bank loan originations had another record year.

Schwab - The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) shows a balance-sheet side to how Schwab earns on client assets. Bank sweep deposits and payables to brokerage clients rose by a total of $42.7 billion, or 14%, from June 30, 2025. The filing presents net interest revenue alongside interest-earning assets and funding sources.

Schwab - The April 2026 monthly activity report (published 2026-05-14) says Schwab earns a fixed net yield on client margin loans ($29.6 billion) and on short credits tied to certain long/short strategies ($30.5 billion).

Edward Jones (advisor-led) - The 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) says net revenue rose 11% to $17,700, primarily on asset-based fee revenue. It attributes that growth to advisory programs, higher average market levels and more client dollars invested in advisory programs. Interest and dividends revenue decreased because lower interest rates reduced income on short-term investments, bank cash balances and reverse repurchase agreements.

Edward Jones (advisor-led) - The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) says six-month net revenue rose 15% to $9,679, primarily on asset-based fee revenue. Advisory programs' average AUC rose 28%, and interest and dividends revenue fell in a lower interest rate environment. The filing says commission-related compensation increased with revenues on which commissions are earned.

Raymond James (advisor-led) - The 1Q26 10-Q (published 2026-05-06) says fees from fee-based accounts are based on the value of client assets. It says they vary by account type and by the level of assets in the client relationship. Most such accounts are billed on balances at the beginning of the quarter, so revenue may not react immediately to changes in asset values.

Bank of America GWIM segment (Merrill plus Private Bank, not Merrill alone) - The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) says fees on assets under management are calculated as a percentage of clients' AUM balances. It says the fees charged "are commonly driven by the breadth of the client's relationship."

gaps.what: Schwab's revenue mix (net interest revenue versus asset management and administration fees versus trading revenue) is not in the evidence provided. The evidence also has no source that directly contrasts Schwab with an advisor-led model, so the comparison above is built from each firm's own disclosures.
gaps.suggested_source: Schwab 10-K or 10-Q net revenue breakdown and net interest margin tables, plus the earnings call transcript
